edge_players.edge_sentence: Dalton Schultz is at about 87.5 receiving yards on 11 targets a game, and 49.5 asks him to lose almost 40 yards of that role against a defense allowing 11.88 YPA in the middle where a tight end works.
edge_players.must_be_true: Schultz plays a full snap share — health is not in the pack and must hold — Stroud starts, and Schultz keeps something near his 22-target share rather than Collins (10) or Hutchinson (15) taking the game. The HOU pass-lean base script has to show up.
edge_players.kills_it: A snap limit or late scratch not in the pack, IND bracketing the tight end after the 22-target trend, or HOU sustaining the run (both backs under 3.0 YPC, the less likely flip) so Stroud only needs about 20 throws. A pure efficiency drop on the same volume is not enough: 5 yards per target on 10 targets still clears 49.5.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Jonathan Taylor is at about 126.5 rush-plus-receiving yards per game (190 rush and 63 receiving) against 106.5, and the combo still works if IND leads on his 21.5 carries or trails into the negative-air checkdowns he already has 8 targets of.
edge_players.must_be_true: Taylor keeps the bellcow role from the pack (43 carries and 8 targets over two games; no snap limit is listed because injuries are absent) and either an 18-plus carry floor or the checkdown receiving holds. This is the combo, not a pure rush bet.
edge_players.kills_it: HOU's 4.12 YPC run defense holds him in the mid-3s on a reduced carry count and the 17% HOU blitz rate means Jones is not forced to dump off, so the 63 receiving yards disappear. A trail script that kills the run without replacing it in the passing game loses 106.5. Price is not saved.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost. Schultz went under 49.5 because the 175 yards were a two-game target peak, Collins and Hutchinson (10 and 15 targets) split the intermediate work, IND used a shell the pack does not chart to take the tight end away, and Stroud's -0.13 EPA with no blitz showed up on the 75% of dropbacks IND did not blitz — five targets, 38 yards. Taylor finished under 106.5 because HOU's 4.12 YPC defense was the real number: 16 carries at 3.7 YPC is 59, and with HOU blitzing only 17% Jones never had to check down, so Taylor added one catch for 8 and the combo died near 67. The Schultz counter is real but weaker than a 22-target, 130-air-yard role against 11.88 middle YPA. The Taylor counter is strong enough that he stays a lean, not a strong, and he drops if inactives cut his snaps.
slip_story: One story: HOU cannot run (Montgomery 2.69 YPC, Marks 2.94) so Stroud throws to Schultz into IND's middle, and IND keeps feeding Taylor on the ground and on checkdowns because Jones has no efficient dropback split. These two win together in a competitive IND-run / HOU-pass game. Do not add HOU running-back overs — those need IND's 5.67 YPC bleed and a HOU run script, the opposite of this base. Do not add Warren or Allen unders; 2.8 to 3.4 yards per target looks fluky and the market already has Warren at 46.5. No total is saved, so this is not a shootout stack and not an under stack. Two legs, no touchdowns.
